newsitem.title: USA: Owens Corning expects 96 oper shr increase.
newsitem.headline: Owens Corning expects 96 oper shr increase.

text.p: Owens Corning said on Tuesday that it is comfortable with a 1996 operating share estimate of between $4.65 per share and $4.75 per share.
Owens Corning Chairman and Chief Executive Glen Hiner said in a statement that its outlook for the rest of the year makes the company comfortable with that projection.
The projections are for fully diluted shares from ongoing operations. In 1995, the company posted earnings of $4.25 per share from ongoing operations.

The company said this year's third-quarter results -- when it reported net income of $80 million, or $1.44 per fully diluted share, versus $70 million, or $1.28 per fully diluted share in the 1995 third quarter -- were driven by acquisitions and its roofing business.

The company's compositive materials segment showed improved margins in this year's third quarter primarily because of improved pricing and productivity in the United States, the company said. However, sales for the segment fell slightly because of weak demand in Europe, the company said.
Sales for composite materials were $274 million for the quarter compared with $287 million for the same period in 1995.

"We have taken appropriate action to adjust short-term capacity while our customers are adjusting their inventories," Hiner said in the statement. "Our built-in flexibility allows us to react quickly to meet customer demand."
